# Robustness details {#sec-app-robustness}

```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import _helpers as H

A = H.rob_section("A")
B = H.rob_section("B")
rowsL = [r for r in H.rob_rows("C") if r["id"].startswith("C4-loco")]
```

This appendix gives the tables behind @sec-robustness. All tables are read from `reports/results/robustness.json`; sections not present are marked as not yet available. Nothing here is used to select a specification.

## Driscoll--Kraay, two-way clustering and CCE designs {#sec-app-dk}

```{python}
#| output: asis
dk = A.get("dk_crosscheck_real", {})
bw = dk.get("bandwidths", {})
if dk:
    parts = []
    for m, v in bw.items():
        parts.append(f"bandwidth m = {m}: maximum relative difference in standard errors {H.sci(v.get('max_rel_diff_se'), 1)}")
    print("Driscoll--Kraay standard errors (Bartlett kernel; small-sample factor as in the project's CR1 convention; $t(26)$ critical values) were cross-checked against `linearmodels.PanelOLS(...).fit(cov_type='kernel')` on the real regressors: " + "; ".join(parts) + f"; coefficients agree to {H.sci(dk.get('max_rel_diff_coefficients'), 1)} relative difference. The two-way clustered variance matrix (Cameron--Gelbach--Miller) was not positive semi-definite and negative eigenvalues were set to zero before the standard errors were read (see the JSON for the eigenvalue).")
else:
    print("> **Not yet available:** Driscoll-Kraay cross-check.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-cce
#| tbl-cap: "CCE designs (Pesaran 2006 pooled; country-specific coefficients on cross-sectional averages; year effects kept). Source: robustness.json, section A."
cce = A.get("cce", {})
rows = []
for k, lab in [("lite", "CCE-lite"), ("full", "CCE-full")]:
    c = cce.get(k)
    if c:
        rows.append({"Version": lab, "CSA variables": c.get("n_csa_variables"), "Added parameters": c.get("added_parameters"),
                     "Total parameters": c.get("n_parameters_total"), "Residual df": c.get("residual_df"),
                     "df exhausted": "yes" if c.get("df_exhausted") else "no"})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), widths=[14, 14, 16, 16, 12, 12])
else:
    H.not_yet("CCE design table")
```

CCE-full adds 260 country-specific coefficients to a sample of 715 observations, so it should be read as a stress test of the specification, not as a preferred model; degrees of freedom are not exhausted (@tbl-app-cce).

## Residual cross-sectional dependence {#sec-app-cd}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-cd
#| tbl-cap: "Residual cross-sectional dependence: Pesaran CD, mean pairwise correlation and mean absolute pairwise correlation, with simulated benchmarks for independent AR(1) errors passed through the same projection. Source: robustness.json, section A."
dep = A.get("dependence", [])
rows = []
for d in dep:
    n1 = d.get("null_ar1", {})
    rows.append({"Residuals": d.get("model"), "CD": H.num(d.get("cd"), 2), "Mean corr.": H.num(d.get("mean_corr"), 3),
                 "Mean abs. corr.": H.num(d.get("mean_abs_corr"), 3),
                 "AR(1) null: mean abs. corr.": H.num(n1.get("mean_abs_corr"), 3),
                 "Excess vs null": H.num(d.get("excess_mean_abs_corr_vs_ar1"), 3)})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), widths=[44, 8, 12, 14, 18, 14])
else:
    H.not_yet("residual dependence table")
```

@tbl-app-cd reports the residual dependence statistics. A caveat applies to the Pesaran CD statistic. Residuals of models with year effects have, by construction, an average pairwise correlation of about $-1/(G-1)$ = `{python} H.num(-1/26, 3)` for $G = 27$ countries, which shifts the statistic to about $-3.7$ even under independence, so the standard normal $p$-value is not informative here. The statistic is therefore reported next to simulated benchmarks, and the mean absolute pairwise correlation is the more informative summary: its excess over the AR(1) benchmark is modest for the OLS and V7 residuals (0.03 to 0.04, two to three simulation standard deviations of the benchmark) and negligible once CCE-full is added. This is not proof that the year effects control common shocks adequately, and residual cross-country dependence may remain, which is consistent with the dependence of the headline's statistical evidence on the inference method (@sec-rob-inference).<!-- CHECKED-STATIC (2026-10-14 against robustness.md, residual dependence table: excess 0.032 and 0.042, benchmark SD 0.014) -->

## Pre-registered diagnostics {#sec-app-diag}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-diag
#| tbl-cap: "Pre-registered diagnostics (reported, never used to select a specification). Source: robustness.json, section B."
rows = []
mw = B.get("modified_wald", {})
for k, lab in [("ols_fe_residuals", "Modified Wald, OLS-FE residuals"), ("v7_residuals", "Modified Wald, V7 residuals")]:
    v = mw.get(k)
    if v:
        rows.append({"Test": lab, "Statistic": H.num(v.get("statistic"), 1), "Result": f"chi-square p {H.sci(v.get('p_value'))}; Monte Carlo p {H.pval(v.get('p_value_mc'), 4)} (null 95th percentile {H.num(v.get('null_q95_statistic'), 1)})"})
w = B.get("wooldridge")
if w:
    rows.append({"Test": "Wooldridge serial correlation", "Statistic": f"F({w.get('df1')}, {w.get('df2')}) = {H.num(w.get('f_statistic'), 1)}", "Result": f"p {H.sci(w.get('p_value'))}; coefficient {H.num(w.get('coefficient'), 3)} (SE {H.num(w.get('se'), 3)}), {w.get('n_pairs')} residual pairs"})
for k, lab in [("cips_capb_constant", "CIPS, CAPB, constant"), ("cips_capb_trend", "CIPS, CAPB, trend"), ("cips_moderator_lag_constant", "CIPS, lagged OLDDEP1, constant"), ("cips_moderator_lag_trend", "CIPS, lagged OLDDEP1, trend")]:
    v = B.get(k)
    if v:
        rows.append({"Test": lab, "Statistic": H.num(v.get("cips"), 3), "Result": f"5% critical value {H.num(v.get('crit_5'), 2)} (simulated); p {H.pval(v.get('p_value_left_tail'), 3)}; unit root {'rejected' if v.get('reject_5pct') else 'not rejected'} at 5%"})
h = B.get("hausman_mundlak")
if h:
    rows.append({"Test": "Hausman, Mundlak form", "Statistic": f"Wald = {H.num(h.get('wald'), 1)} (q = {h.get('q')})", "Result": f"F({h.get('q')}, {h.get('df2')}) p {H.sci(h.get('p_value_f'))}"})
hc = B.get("hausman_classical")
if hc:
    rows.append({"Test": "Hausman, classical", "Statistic": f"H = {H.num(hc.get('statistic'), 2)} (df {hc.get('df')})", "Result": f"p {H.pval(hc.get('p_value'), 3)}; not interpretable: random-effects variance is {H.num(hc.get('re_effects_variance'), 1)} and {hc.get('n_negative_eigenvalues')} eigenvalues of V_FE - V_RE are negative"})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), align="lll", widths=[34, 22, 70])
else:
    H.not_yet("section B diagnostics")
```

@tbl-app-diag lists the diagnostics, @tbl-app-vif the variance inflation factors and @tbl-app-bins the binned estimates. The modified Wald statistic over-rejects in short panels, which is why a Monte Carlo $p$-value under independent normal errors with this panel's layout is shown beside the chi-square value. The classical Hausman statistic is not interpretable here, and the Mundlak form is the Hausman result.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-vif

                       "VIF on raw columns": [H.num(x, 2) for x in v.get("vif_raw", [])]})
    df["Regressor"] = df["Regressor"].str.replace("_", "\\_", regex=False)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-bins

                     "Binned effect of $W^S$ [95% CI]": f"{H.num(b.get('binned_estimate'), 2)} {H.ival(b.get('binned_ci_lo'), b.get('binned_ci_hi'), 2)}",
                     "Linear prediction": H.num(b.get("linear_prediction"), 2)})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), widths=[12, 6, 20, 8, 12, 30, 12])
else:
    H.not_yet("binned linearity tables")
```

```{python}
#| include: false
lb, lw = B.get("binned_between", {}), B.get("binned_within", {})
```

The lead placebo of @sec-rob-diagnostics is tabulated in @tbl-app-lead. Linearity tests (adding the second and third bin interactions) give $p$ = `{python} H.pval(lb.get("linearity_p"), 2)` for the between and `{python} H.pval(lw.get("linearity_p"), 2)` for the within component. No bin has thin support (fewer than five exposed countries), but each bin rests on only eight to ten countries.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-lead
#| tbl-cap: "Lead placebo (V7; W^S_lead is the share of the year inside months 13-24 before a scheduled election). Source: robustness.json, section B."
rows = []
for k, lab in [("lead_placebo", "As specified (1995-2021)"), ("lead_placebo_to_2020", "To 2020")]:
    d = B.get(k)
    if d:
        rows.append({"Sample": lab, "N": d.get("n_obs"), "Lead coefficient [95% interval]": H.est_ci(d.get("lead"), 3), "p": H.pval(d.get("lead", {}).get("p"), 3),
                     "$\\beta_S$ in the augmented model": H.est_ci(d.get("beta_S"), 3), "$\\gamma_B$ in the augmented model": H.est_ci(d.get("gamma_B"), 3)})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), widths=[36, 6, 28, 8, 28, 28])
else:
    H.not_yet("lead placebo")
```

## Leave-one-country-out fits {#sec-app-loco}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-app-loco
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-country-out fits (V7, wild-cluster bootstrap-t with B = 999 each; pp of potential GDP). Source: robustness.json, section C."
rows = []
for r in rowsL:
    b, g = r["targets"]["beta_S"], r["targets"]["gamma_B"]
    rows.append({"Left out": r["id"].split("-")[-1], "$\\beta_S$ [95% interval]": H.est_ci(b, 3), "p": H.pval(b.get("p"), 3), "Reading": H.reading_of(b),
                 "$\\gamma_B$ [95% interval]": H.est_ci(g, 3), "Reading ": H.reading_of(g)})
if rows:
    H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), align="lrrlrl", widths=[8, 28, 8, 16, 28, 22])
else:
    H.not_yet("leave-one-out table")
```

@tbl-app-loco lists every fit; none is selected, and the table is not a ranking. Bootstrap $p$-values for these fits use only 999 replications and are correspondingly coarse.
